Availability Search Overview ​

The AvailabilitySearch Livewire component is the main component that you'll use to add the reservation functionality to your site. It allows the user to search for a date or date range, by specific rate and select the quantity that they want to book.

In this page, we'll go over the basics of how to use the component, and then we'll explain how to use it to search for availability of a single entry or how to pair it with Livewire Filters or Statamic's Collection Tag in order to search for all available entries for a specific date or dates.

Component basics ​

In its most simple form, you can include the AvailabilitySearch component in your Antlers templates like so:

antlers
{{ livewire:availability-search calendar="range" }}

More often than not, you'll also want to include the AvailabilityResults component to display the results of the search and the "Book now" button that starts the checkout process.

TIP

Each search that the user makes is saved in the session (under the key resrv-search), so that their search persists between page loads.

Component properties ​

Of course, there are quite a few properties that you can set depending on the use case. Here's a list of all the available properties:

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
calendarstring"single"The calendar type to use. single selects a single date, range selects a date range.
livebooleantrueWhen enabled, the component automatically updates the results when the user changes any value of their search. When disabled, the component only updates when the user clicks the "Search" button.
ratesbooleanfalseWhen enabled, the rate selector is rendered so the user can pick a rate. Pass :rates="true". (Replaces the v5 advanced property: it's now a plain boolean.)
anyRatebooleanfalseUsable when searching for multiple entries. When enabled, an unselected rate is sent as "any" and the results return the cheapest rate that is available. Search is also allowed without dates. Pass :any-rate="true".
enableQuantitybooleanfalseWhen enabled, a quantity control is added so that the user can book more than one product at once.
redirectTostringnullIf live mode is disabled, the page to redirect to when the user clicks "Search".
resetOnBootbooleanfalseWhen enabled, on mount the component resets the quantity to 1 and the rate to null, ignoring whatever is saved in the session. Useful to discard a stale search on a landing page.
overrideRatesarray[]A rate_id => label map that overrides the rates resolved from the database for this entry/collection.
showAvailabilityOnCalendarbooleanfalseShow availability & pricing information on the calendar. Usable only when browsing a specific entry.
entrystringnullNeeds to be a Statamic Entry ID. Used to resolve the per-entry rate labels and required when showAvailabilityOnCalendar is enabled. Optional for collection-wide search.
ratesBlueprintstringnullOptional. Carries the collection.blueprint reference when needed (mainly for the Livewire Filters path). Not required for normal single/collection search, since rates are now collection-scoped database records.
viewstring"availability-search"Override the view that's used to render the component. Really useful when you want different versions of the AvailabilitySearch component on different pages. Expects a name.blade.php file in the /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire folder.

UPGRADING FROM v5

Several properties were renamed in v6 as part of the move to the Rates system: advanced → rates, anyAdvanced → anyRate, overrideProperties → overrideRates. The boot-reset property is resetOnBoot (the v5 docs mistakenly called it resetAdvancedOnBoot). See Upgrading to v6 for the full list.

Customizing ​

The design of the Availability Search component is very basic by default, since it's meant to be modified to fit your layout. To modify it, make sure you've published the views during checkout and edit the /resources/views/vendor/statamic-resrv/livewire/availability-search.blade.php file.

In the same path, inside the components folder, you can find and customize the Blade components that are used by the Availability Search component. The rate selector lives in components/availability-rates.blade.php.

Usage ​

The component can be used in three different ways:

  1. As a standalone search form that redirects to a results page. This is something that you'd probably use on the homepage of a site. To use it this way, you can set live to false and redirectTo to the Entry ID of the page you want to redirect to.
  2. As a search form inside a single Entry. When you want your user to search for a single Entry, usually on the aforementioned Entry's page. Follow along at single entry for examples.
  3. As a search form on an index page. When you want the user to input their search and list all available Entries. You can find your options on the multiple entries page.

Passing data to checkout ​

There are some cases where you might want to pass some data to the checkout page before the user gets there. A good example is the Guests component where we pass along the number of guests to the checkout page. To achieve that you can bind the control you want to use to the data.customer.handle property of the AvailabilitySearch component. Just make sure to create the appropriate fields in your checkout form. If you don't want to allow the user to edit them, remember to set them as hidden fields in your blueprint.

Disabling dates of the week ​

In some cases you might want to disable specific days of the week. To do so, you need to edit your availability-search.blade.php file (make sure you publish your views during installation or by running php artisan vendor:publish --tag=resrv-checkout-views) and add a disabledDays array to the x-resrv::availability-dates component like so:

blade
<x-resrv::availability-dates
    :$calendar
    disabledDays='["Saturday", "Sunday"]'
    :errors="$errors"
/>

The array uses full English day names (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday).
